video_title: ESPN’s Shams Charania Talks Wemby, LeBron, Giannis, NBA Draft & More w/ Rich Eisen | Full Interview

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's MVP win fuels Victor Wembanyama's competitive drive
quotes.excerpt: the competitive motivation factor that it has undoubtedly for a guy like Victor Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: That's real. That's why, you know, you think about how big of a deal, how big of a story on its face, just Shai Gilgeous-Alexander winning back-to-back MVP awards, on its face alone, that's a massive story. 14th player ever to do so. You look at his numbers over the course of the last year, especially this season, I mean, he's in rarefied air. He's in the same category as Michael Jordan, back-to-back MVPs, first guard since Steph Curry, first back-to-back MVP since Nikola Jokic. But just what he's done year after year since he's been in Oklahoma City, his rise, it's a massive story in and of itself, but I think the other dual component to it is the competitive motivation factor that it has undoubtedly for a guy like Victor Wembanyama.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama is a uniquely focused and driven young star
quotes.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama is just a different type of specimen and force.
quotes.quote: Anyone that knows Victor Wembanyama, he's as focused, as driven of a young star as we've seen come into the league. I think Cooper Flagg is very similar in that mold as far as just genuine focus on basketball, being great, and hating to lose and trying to be great and amazing at all costs. And there's a few other players in the league, we can go on, Anthony Edwards I think you can put right up there, Luka Doncic is someone that's been a high-level competitor as well. But Victor Wembanyama is just a different type of specimen and force.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's unique off-court interests and dedication to self-growth
quotes.excerpt: he's not interested necessarily in some of the lifestyle components that come with being in the NBA.
quotes.quote: That's how everyone around him has known him, is just how focused and how driven he is. But he's also like he's not interested necessarily in some of the lifestyle components that come with being in the NBA or making a ton of money or being famous, right? Like his interests, Ramona Shelburne put up a great story today on ESPN, very well researched, well reported. I need to read the whole thing. I've seen different parts of it. But this is a dude that like is fascinated by obviously we know his lifestyle with the monks last summer and training with Hakeem Olajuwon and spending time with Kevin Garnett and picking Kevin Garnett's mind. Like he had weeks of just like self-growth last offseason. Like there was no, there was no bones to pick with how he wanted to handle his summer.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs' focus on Victor Wembanyama's health and development since his early days
quotes.excerpt: The only thing a player of that size, that height is just the health, right?
quotes.quote: I have been around that orbit with him a little bit since I mean he was like 16, 17 years old in the back of a car of one of his agents driving him around in France. And I remember his agent at one point was like, 'Hey, I have this kid Victor sitting in the back. He's going to be the best player in the world one day.' And at the time he was like 16 years old. So this is someone who people that have known him, have scouted him, have felt like he's going to be that next thing. The only thing a player of that size, that height is just the health, right? And obviously it was unfortunate he had the blood clot last year, but he's been for the most part, he missed a few weeks with a calf strain in December. But for the most part, he hit the 65-game quota, first unanimous defensive player of the year award winner. And that organization in San Antonio, I don't know if there's a better organization for him to just plop into as a number one overall pick. They're going to be as guarded and as sharp and as focused on his development and his health as any organization in the league.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Gregg Popovich remains the Spurs' decision-maker, guiding future leadership
quotes.excerpt: Gregg Popovich is still very much a part of Spurs operations. He is the decision-maker.

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: We have to remember, Gregg Popovich is still very much a part of Spurs operations. He is the, like I, when I broke last summer that he was no longer the head coach, it was like, yeah, he's no longer the head coach, but he's the President of Basketball Operations of this team. Like he is the decision-maker. Brian Wright, their general manager, he does everything on a day-to-day level. He's been the one making the draft picks, he's the one that's been making the trades and the acquisitions. But, you know, RC Buford, the CEO, Gregg Popovich as head coach for all those years, now he's the president. Those guys are the hierarchy of this organization. Those guys are the Godfathers of this organization. And honestly, the way I look at the Spurs right now is like you have the Pop-RC relationship, to me, with the Spurs, with the Spurs are trying to emulate now, is the same thing with the next people up, and that's Brian Wright as general manager and Mitch Johnson as the head coach, where this is not just for a two, three, four-year shelf life. Like they want to have the same grandfathered dual partnership for years and years to come, and that obviously starts from Pop and then RC Buford and then trickles down.

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Eisen
text_blocks.text: I'm not going to rest until I find out the exact conversation that they had. I'm so fascinated by it, man. If I, if you don't mind me tasking you to do something.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City Thunder maintain draft optionality, often trading up for preferred players
quotes.excerpt: The Thunder yearly have multiple first-round picks, multiple second-round picks in every draft.
quotes.quote: The Thunder yearly have multiple first-round picks, multiple second-round picks in every draft. I mean, knowing how the Thunder have operated, talking to other teams about how they operate, they keep all options open. Something like trading up or trading, like these things don't necessarily really happen until we're on draft night. You have to see who's available on the board. I mean, the Thunder have routinely, every year, every couple years, they'll make a move where they move up because they like someone, you know, at, at, you know, let's say, you know, they have the number 12th pick I think in this year's draft. Like if they like someone at 10 or nine or eight and they can move up, like they'll, they'll look at doing that. Or even 11, even moving up one spot. So I think the Thunder, Sam Presti, his front office, they, they've kept their their optionality as we get closer to draft night.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Top of the NBA Draft remains uncertain with multiple teams considering several prospects
quotes.excerpt: I think there's a lot of questions about the top of this draft.

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: I think there's a lot of questions about the top of this draft. And from Washington, Utah, Memphis, Chicago, I think there's a feel of who, you know, is generally in that mix. AJ Dybantsa, Darren Peterson, Caleb Wilson, Cam Boozer, but I, I think the order is still very much up in the air. I think that Washington at number one, knowing that front office, they're going to consider three, four, five players for that spot. I think Utah at number two is going to consider four, five people for that, for that number two spot. So this is a draft where I, I think we, we could see, I don't know if surprise is the right word, but if Darren Peterson goes number one, like is that going to surprise people?

text_blocks.speaker: Rich Eisen
text_blocks.text: I don't think so either. I don't think so either.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo is ready to part ways with the Milwaukee Bucks
quotes.excerpt: Yannis for a period of months has made it clear to the Bucks that he is ready to part ways.
quotes.quote: Yannis's situation has been playing out for now we're at 12 months by the time, you know, assuming he is traded. And right now, this is so, Rich, this is where everything is at. The Milwaukee Bucks are officially open for business. They are engaging with teams, they're talking to teams, they're getting teams' best offers between now and the NBA draft, and they will make a decision. The biggest point that you need to know in all this, Rich, is Yannis for a period of months has made it clear to the Bucks, to the parties that need to know, that he is ready, he believes the time has come for both sides to part ways, to move on from each other. And what I've learned since Jimmy Haslam came out and said, 'Listen, it's going to be either he's going to commit to an extension in June or we're going to trade him in June,' is that nothing has changed about his stance. And so that would lead you to believe that the Bucks will then obviously seriously consider these offers that they are officially open for business for.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James expected to play one more season, with Lakers as preferred destination
quotes.excerpt: All the indications I've gotten over the course of the year is that he's going to play one more season.
quotes.quote: LeBron's future is a little bit different because LeBron is 41 years old, just finished his 23rd season. He's going to take the next few weeks to figure out exactly how he wants potentially his final year to play out. All the indications I've gotten over the course of the year is that he's going to play one more season. The where, the how much of it all, like that, that's all obviously going to be a factor. Is it going to be LA? That's got to be probably his preference if he wants to be home and stay, you know, as far as where his home base is now. And the Lakers have made it clear that they want him back. And so we'll see how that mutual potential interest culminates over the next month or so. But the one thing I do know is that multiple contenders are already kind of circling here. Like if LeBron is really going to hit the open market and decide and have a true free agency, he's not going to have a shortage of teams that feel like, 'Listen, we'll go get LeBron, we'll plug him in as our starting power forward or small forward, and like let's go try to win a ring.'

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Masai Ujiri initiates a fresh start for the Mavericks by firing Jason Kidd
quotes.excerpt: Masai Ujiri, the new team president and alternate governor coming in and implementing a totally fresh start.
quotes.quote: Jason Kidd was let go as the head coach. He was fired as head coach. He has, he's on the hook for four years, $45 million. The Mavs will pay him out on that unless he gets a coaching job somewhere else. And that there'll be some kind of an offset. But this is Masai Ujiri, the new team president and alternate governor coming in and implementing a totally fresh start. And all the residue of the Luka Doncic trade over the last seven months. Nico Harrison fired. Anthony Davis traded for salaries and a few draft picks. Jason Kidd fired. And conversations that Masai Ujiri's had, ownership's had, the research and the information gathering that they've done in the lead up to this, it's, it's unquestionably a part of it that that Jason Kidd had a level of support for the Luka Doncic trade. But even beyond that, my understanding is, you know, the environment, the culture that's been developed over the last year or so. Masai Ujiri just wanted a clean slate from it. And that's what he did. That's what he's, he started his, his implementation for. And everyone now knows, there's a new sheriff in town, it's Masai Ujiri. And I think moving forward, you're going to see a comprehensive coaching search. And Masai Ujiri will, will find who he feels will be his best long-term coach and partner for him.
